name: Citizens Financial Group, Inc.
moat_justification: Moderate large-regional moat: a scaled deposit franchise ($185.6B deposits, consumer deposits 64% of the total) with improving returns (ROTCE 13.9% in Q2 2026, guided path to 16-18% by end-2027) and a real Private Bank growth engine ($17.8B spot deposits) — against a commodity banking product with no structural pricing power (NIM 3.17% is earned, not owned), full exposure to the credit cycle (provisions are the swing factor) and the rate cycle (current NIM expansion leans on fading swap-termination and repricing tailwinds), regulatory capital limits on growth and capital return (CET1 10.4% at Q2 2026), and money-center scale competitors (efficiency ratio still 61.1%).
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.9%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low

OVERRIDE_APPLIED:capex — filing gap in the last 3 FY filled by a judgment override (filing: Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed 2026-02-12), Consolidated Statements of Cash Flows, investing activities line 'Capital expenditures, net': $174M for FY2025, with $122M for FY2024 and $172M for FY2023 in the same statement (all in $ millions; corroborated in EDGAR companyfacts under the tag PaymentsForProceedsFromProductiveAssets, which the engine does not read, with identical values $174M/$122M/$172M)); an override never replaces a filed value — see overrides_applied and override_impact
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.5x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
HIGH_NET_DEBT: net debt is 5.0x normalized OE — levered OE can vanish fast; stress the bear cases
one_liner: Large regional bank in a genuine earnings recovery, moat 5/10 — TTM OE $5.13/sh is an 8.35% yield at $61.46, but on through-cycle growth starts the weighted IRR is 12.63% (IV@15% $49.38), so it clears 15% only below ~$49; bank-model mismatch, confidence low.
moat_for: Deposit franchise at scale — $185.6B period-end deposits at Q2 2026 funding $147.5B of loans (spot loan-to-deposit 79.5%); consumer deposits 64% of total vs ~56% peer average per management
Improving returns — ROTCE 13.9% in Q2 2026 vs 11.0% a year earlier, guided path to 16-18% by end-2027; NIM 3.17% in Q2 2026, guided toward 3.25% in Q4 2026
Private Bank build-out — spot deposits $17.8B at Q2 2026, contributing $0.15 of Q2 EPS, a fee-rich growth engine inside a commodity business
Credit discipline — net charge-offs 0.37% of average loans in Q2 2026, down from 0.48% a year earlier; allowance coverage 1.48% of loans and 152% of nonaccruals (0.97% of loans)
Consistent buybacks — diluted shares shrinking 2.9%/yr; $700-850M of repurchases guided for 2026; treasury stock purchased $600M in FY2025 per the 10-K
moat_against: Commodity product — deposits and loans are fungible; NIM 3.17% is earned through the cycle, not structural pricing power
Credit-cycle exposure — provisions are the swing factor (FY2025 provision for credit losses $608M, added back inside OCF); a recession turns the bear cases fast
Capital-constrained growth — CET1 10.4% at Q2 2026, managed to ~10.5%; loan growth, dividends and buybacks compete for the same capital, and Basel III endgame requirements are still evolving
Rate sensitivity — the current NIM expansion leans on terminated-swap benefits and fixed-rate asset repricing, tailwinds that fade; deposit repricing pressure is outside management control
Efficiency / scale disadvantage — Q2 2026 efficiency ratio 61.1%, still well behind the money-center banks' technology and compliance scale
